description: Recording and routing templates for Marju's optional voice-guided CV. No audio files, acoustic features, or recognition implementation are included.

commandRecording.notes: Record only the command's phrase, once per file. These are initial reference samples, not a speaker-independent recognizer. Text aliases are not acoustic samples; each alias needs its own recordings if used by an audio-template matcher. Normalize audio consistently when the matcher is implemented.

runtimePlan.recognitionThresholdNote: Calibrate acceptance and best-versus-second-best margin on held-out recordings from different speakers and noise conditions. Reject uncertain matches rather than always choosing the closest template.
runtimePlan.navigation: Maintain a history stack. Back returns to the previous menu. Menu returns to main. Repeat replays the current narration without changing history. Help reads the current menu's choices. Stop stops narration and listening, then optionally plays goodbye; physical stop must remain available during playback.
runtimePlan.privacy: Proposed local matching. Do not upload or retain visitor recordings without a separate disclosed design and consent.

clips.text: Hello! Welcome to my page. I'm Marju, and this is my interactive CV. On the page, my education lives in a stack of books, my work experience is packed into an old suitcase, and my projects are potatoes! You don't need to see those objects to explore them. What would you like to know about me? Say about me, education, projects, work experience, skills, or languages. Use the listen button when you're ready to answer. Say help whenever you need to hear the choices again.

I'm Marju, a junior software developer with professional experience in software testing, application support, and Microsoft Dynamics NAV-based finance systems. In my personal projects, I work with C plus plus, C sharp, dot net, Go, Python, and databases. Two of my ongoing projects are Mental Model Graph, a tool for understanding complex software systems, and Goatly, a learning platform for children. Outside software development, I also create children's stories for my son.

Welcome to my bookshelf! Each book represents a part of my education. There's the University of Skövde, the University of Tartu, Lexicon, Komvux, and my gymnasium education in Estonia. There are also loose papers representing standalone courses in art, design, and three-dimensional modelling. Which would you like to hear about? Say Skövde, Tartu, Lexicon, Komvux, gymnasium, or standalone courses. Use the listen button when you're ready.

I have a bachelor's degree in Informatics from the University of Skövde, comprising one hundred and eighty university credits. The degree combined transferred studies from Estonia with additional coursework in Sweden. My thesis explored email classification using Latent Dirichlet Allocation and a Random Forest classifier. I investigated how additional information affected classification accuracy. My courses included software testing, algorithms and data structures, systems thinking, quantitative methods, and English.

I studied Informatics at the University of Tartu in Estonia between two thousand and seven and two thousand and ten. My studies covered programming, mathematics, databases, software engineering, artificial intelligence, operating systems, and software testing. I also studied drawing, painting, user interface design, digital painting, and multimedia. It was a combination of technical and creative subjects.

My CV currently lists an ongoing full-stack developer programme through Lexicon and Luleå University of Technology. It is a forty-five-week, full-time remote programme combining practical programming, an academic phase, and a workplace placement. The subjects include C sharp and dot net, object-oriented programming, relational databases, software testing, web development, REST APIs, and Agile development.
Between two thousand and thirteen and two thousand and fifteen, I studied at Komvux. I completed English six and seven, as well as Swedish as a Second Language, levels one through three.
I completed my upper secondary education in Estonia in two thousand and seven. My subjects included mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and natural science.

In two thousand and sixteen, I took additional university courses in creative subjects. At Luleå University of Technology, I studied digital painting and idea visualisation, as well as game design. At Uppsala University, I studied three-dimensional modelling and visualisation with ZBrush. At the University of Gävle, I studied three-dimensional modelling and animation in an open-source environment.

You've reached my potato bag! Each potato is a different project. There's Goatly, Mental Model Graph, and Frog Game. Goatly is a children's learning platform. Mental Model Graph helps developers understand source code. Frog Game is a playful puzzle game. Which potato would you like to explore? Say Goatly, Mental Model Graph, or Frog Game. Use the listen button when you're ready.

Goatly is my ongoing concept-based language-learning platform for children with language delays and multilingual backgrounds. It connects educators, caregivers, and the languages spoken at home. The idea is to make visual communication support more engaging through personalised characters, voices, playful activities, and learning journeys connected to real-world experiences. The project began with Go and Encore. I'm now rebuilding it in C sharp and dot net using Clean Architecture. My work includes permissions, child-safe access to media, databases, automated testing, and maintainable system boundaries. A public code example and a live demo are linked in the project section.

Mental Model Graph, or M M G, is my ongoing source-code analysis project. It turns C plus plus codebases into navigable graphs, helping developers explore components, relationships, tests, and supporting evidence. I use C plus plus twenty, CMake, Python, and Tree-sitter. The project currently runs as a locally built command-line application. I also created a custom testing framework to keep required behaviours visible and support systematic testing. A public code example is linked in the project section.

Frog Game is a silly, soothing puzzle game for children and adults. It offers a little logical challenge and a calm escape during stressful moments. I originally built it from scratch in Unity and C sharp and released it as an Android application. Unfortunately, I lost the latest version of the original game. Using the visual and audio assets I still had, I created a similar browser game with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The browser version recreates the core puzzle logic rather than being a direct Unity export. You can find the playable version in the project section.

Let's open my work-experience suitcase. From twenty twenty-four to twenty twenty-five, I worked as a QA Engineer at Silverspin in Skövde. I created Playwright tests and manually tested a sportsbook, finding defects that were corrected before release. From twenty twenty to twenty twenty-four, I was an Application Support Consultant at Aptic. I handled support requests, wrote documentation, and investigated errors in Microsoft Dynamics NAV export files. From twenty seventeen to twenty twenty, I worked as a System Developer at Asitis. My work included manual testing, requirements, investigating defects in C slash A L code, and improving testing methods. Earlier, I worked at a garden nursery, caring for plants and selling products at markets. I also worked as a playhost for Tallink, organising children's activities and hosting karaoke for adults.

My skills combine development, testing, and application support. In software testing, I have experience with manual, functional, regression, unit, and integration testing. I also work with test planning, debugging, requirements, and defect investigation. My development work includes C plus plus twenty, C sharp and dot net, Python, and SQL. Through my projects, I work with software architecture, web APIs, databases, authentication, and automated testing. I have used Playwright for browser testing and Git and GitHub for version control. My application-support experience includes customer communication, technical documentation, troubleshooting, and Microsoft Dynamics NAV-based finance systems.

I speak four languages. Estonian is my native language. I have professional proficiency in English and Swedish, and elementary proficiency in German. You can hear a recording of me speaking each language. Say Estonian, English, Swedish, or German. Use the listen button when you're ready.

What would you like to explore next? Say back to return to the previous menu, menu for all sections, or repeat to hear this again. Say stop to end the audio tour. Use the listen button when you're ready to answer.

You can explore about me, education, projects, work experience, skills, or languages. Say the name of the section you want. You can also say back, menu, repeat, or stop. Use the listen button before speaking. You can use the buttons or your keyboard instead.
Sorry, I didn't catch that. Please use the listen button and say your choice again, or say help to hear the available options. You can also choose using the page's buttons or your keyboard.
I didn't hear a choice. Take your time. Use the listen button when you're ready to speak, or choose a section using your keyboard.
Voice input isn't available right now. You can still explore the tour using the page's buttons or your keyboard and listen to the recordings.
Thank you for exploring my CV! You can continue browsing the page, visit my LinkedIn or GitHub, or start the audio tour again. Goodbye for now!
